name: Lokmam Köz (Schanze)
desc: Susannenstraße 16. Blogger's #2: big portions, intense flavours, Falstaff gold medal; 4.8★ with 8,400+ reviews per the same source.
note: Closest big-name pick to the Schanze skatepark (Rote Flora).

name: Kardelen (Neustadt)
desc: Steinwegpassage 6, central near the Michel. Cheap (1–10 €), fast service, queue is normal; free flatbread at the counter per the source.
note: Best walkable option between Landungsbrücken and the city centre.

name: Köz Antep (St. Pauli)
desc: Clemens-Schultz-Straße 26, a few minutes from the Reeperbahn. Owner makes the döner himself, without the usual German seasoning — authentic Turkish style; the lahmacun is praised too. Not everyone's taste.

name: Kebab House Kurtulan (Bahrenfeld)
desc: Leverkusenstraße 2. Blogger's #1 'best döner in Hamburg': fresh spit daily, house-made avocado sauce, queue out the door at lunch. TAKEAWAY ONLY.
note: Out in Bahrenfeld — plan a short ride (also near Altona/Övelgönne side of the ferry route).

name: Batman (Steindamm)
desc: Steindamm 58, St. Georg near the main station. Named after the Turkish city, not the superhero. House-made sauces, fresh flatbread daily.

name: Döner Queen (Winterhude)
desc: Jarrestraße 57. Huge portions, juicy meat, vegan seitan option, free tea after the meal.
note: Near the Barmbek gaming spots (Cosmos Arcade / Retro Spiele Club).

name: Traum Döner (Hammerbrook)
desc: Spaldingstraße 55. Rated 4.9★ (479 reviews) and #1 on the hamburglist.com ranking — a second opinion to the blog list.
note: Close to I-Punkt Skateland (Hammerbrook).

name: Honest Kebab (Ballindamm)
desc: Ballindamm 40 (Europa Passage). Premium 100 % grass-fed beef, no additives; owned by YouTuber 'Holle 21614'. Pricier.

name: Sphinx Döner (Landwehr)
desc: Landwehr 39, Eilbek/Hohenfelde. Old-school döner-shack feel, cheap, outdoor seating.

name: Falafelstern (Schanze)
desc: Schanzenstraße 111. Best vegan döner/falafel per the source — handy if Irena joins another time.

name: Kelle Skatepark (Loogeplatz)
desc: Eppendorf, right next to U-Bahn Kellinghusenstraße. 870 m², room for ~60 skaters; concrete.
note: Easy U-Bahn trip (U1/U3).

name: Skatepark an der Roten Flora (Schanze)
desc: Behind the Rote Flora: cradle, micro ramp, rainbow coping, rollins. Concrete. Small but characterful, right in the Schanze.
note: Pair with Lokmam Köz / Falafelstern.

name: I-Punkt Skateland (Hammerbrook)
desc: 1,500 m² covered hall + 1,800 m² outdoor area: street course, bowl, mini ramp, halfpipe. Weather-proof option.
note: Hours per hamburg.de: Mon/Tue/Thu 15–20, Wed/Fri 15–24, Sat/Sun 13–20. Entry free Mon–Thu in term time; Fri–Sun under 18: 3 €, adults 4 €. Check the site before going.

name: Skatepark Wilhelmsburg (Inselpark)
desc: Former IGS garden-show grounds: ~1,700 m² of smooth concrete, ramps, rails, ledges, and a ~2 m deep bowl (the highlight).
note: Further south; S-Bahn to Wilhelmsburg. Best 'proper' park for a skateboard-focused trip.

name: Skatepark Gleisbogen (Barmbek-Nord)
desc: Opened 13 Sept 2024 under the elevated U-Bahn viaduct: quarter pipes, banks, London gap, pyramid with wallie ledge/rail, flat rail, plus a pumptrack.
note: OSM calls it 'Am Gleisdreieck'; matched to hamburg.de's park by location. Close to Cosmos Arcade and Retro Spiele Club.

name: Bunker Skatepark (Eimsbüttel)
desc: Concrete skate area listed in OpenStreetMap as 'Bunker Skatepark'.
note: Little info beyond OSM — treat as a bonus stop.

name: Skatepark Lenzsiedlung (Lokstedt)
desc: Reopened summer 2023 after renovation: improved surface, modern elements, ~300 m², wheelchair-accessible.
note: Position geocoded from the street address (approx.).

name: Skatepark Holstenstraße (St. Pauli)
desc: Mini ramp with halfpipe, street section, pyramids, copings, bank, transition (per hamburg.de).
note: Position taken from the nearest concrete skate pitch in OSM — verify on arrival. Walkable from the Reeperbahn area.

name: Planten un Blomen skate area (Neustadt)
desc: The ice rink becomes a 4,300 m² skate area, roughly April to end of Sept / mid-Oct.
note: ⚠ SEASONAL — likely closed now (it's November). Pin is the park centre.

name: Skatepark Rissen
desc: Forest setting: pipe, quarter, wallride, rail, curbs, banks, manual pad. Quiet.
note: Far west — only if you have a free afternoon.

name: Allerfornia Skatepark (Neuallermöhe)
desc: Varied obstacles plus a 400 m² trend-sports area with slackline and calisthenics. Free, run by TSG Bergedorf.
note: Far east — low priority.

name: Mantis Skateshop
desc: Skate shop in the city centre (OSM). Good for a stop if he needs bearings, grip or a new deck.

name: Lobby Skateshop
desc: Skate shop near Planten un Blomen (OSM).

name: Landungsbrücken – Pier 3 (ferry start)
desc: Boarding point for HVV harbour ferry Line 62 (Landungsbrücken → Altona Fischmarkt → Dockland → Neumühlen/Övelgönne → Bubendey-Ufer → Finkenwerder). It's regular public transport, so it's cheap and unscripted — a 'mini harbour tour'.
note: Ride on a normal hvv ticket; timetable on hvv.de / hvv app / Google Maps. Weekend frequency in summer is higher than now — check the live timetable.

name: HADAG harbour tours
desc: If you want commentary and a proper Hafenrundfahrt, HADAG runs dedicated harbour tours from the same piers.
note: Same area as Landungsbrücken; pin placed on Pier 3. Check seasonal schedule.

name: Fischmarkt Altona (ferry stop)
desc: Stop on Line 62. Historic fish-auction hall and bistro Liberté right at the pier with a view to the Elbphilharmonie. (The famous fish market itself runs Sunday mornings.)

name: Neumühlen / Övelgönne (ferry stop)
desc: Get off here for the Elbe beach promenade in Övelgönne with its museum harbour of old ships (Museumshafen). Great place to skip a stop and walk back.

name: Museumshafen Övelgönne
desc: Open-air harbour of historic ships on the Elbe.

name: Finkenwerder (end of Line 62)
desc: Terminus of the route — the Airbus works are across the water; a classic round trip back to Landungsbrücken.

name: Alter Elbtunnel (St. Pauli Elbtunnel)
desc: Historic pedestrian/vehicle tunnel under the Elbe starting beside the Landungsbrücken — easy add-on to the ferry.

name: Rickmer Rickmers (museum ship)
desc: Historic three-masted museum ship moored at Landungsbrücken.

name: Cap San Diego (museum ship)
desc: Large museum cargo ship at the Überseebrücke.

name: St. Michaelis (Michel)
desc: Hamburg's landmark baroque church.

name: Speicherstadt
desc: Historic warehouse district (UNESCO World Heritage), good to walk through towards HafenCity.

name: Internationales Maritimes Museum
desc: Maritime history museum in HafenCity.

name: Deutsches Hafenmuseum
desc: Museum of port history on the Kleiner Grasbrook.
note: Website didn't respond during my check — verify the link/opening times.

name: Miniatur Wunderland
desc: World's largest model railway — a crowd-pleaser, especially with a gamer/tech-minded teen.
note: Book ahead; it's often sold out on weekends.

name: Retro Spiele Club (playable museum)
desc: Playable museum of computers, consoles and software from the last 50 years. Visit during opening hours without registration. Moved from Horn (closed 2025) to Fuhlsbüttler Str. 490.
note: ⚠ HOURS: Mon/Thu/Fri 15–21, Sat 13–18; CLOSED Sunday. Under-18s must be accompanied (fine with you). Only Saturday works on a weekend trip. Verify on the site.

name: Cosmos Arcade (Hamburger Meile)
desc: 30+ arcade machines, racing simulators, air hockey and pinball (incl. Jurassic Park).
note: Hamburger Str. 39, Barmbek-Süd. Check opening times on the site.

name: Beatles-Platz
desc: Tribute plaza at the Reeperbahn end of Große Freiheit with steel silhouettes of the five early Beatles.
note: Start of a short Beatles walk — everything below is within a few minutes on foot.

name: Indra Club (Große Freiheit 64)
desc: Where the then-unknown Beatles played their first Hamburg gigs in 1960 after being invited by Bruno Koschmider.

name: Kaiserkeller (Große Freiheit 36)
desc: One of the four Reeperbahn-area clubs the Beatles played 1960–62.

name: Star-Club site (Große Freiheit 39)
desc: The Star-Club, the most famous of the Beatles' Hamburg venues.

name: Top Ten Club site (Reeperbahn 136)
desc: The Beatles' fourth Hamburg venue.

name: Bambi Kino (Paul-Roosen-Straße)
desc: Cinema in a quiet side street where the Beatles were lodged in two windowless rooms next to the men's toilet.

name: Panik City (Udo Lindenberg)
desc: Multimedia museum experience about German rock star Udo Lindenberg and his Hamburg link (Hotel Atlantic, Reeperbahn).
note: Ticketed (~24.50 € listed on hamburg-travel for the morning tour). Check availability.

name: Molotow
desc: Well-known Reeperbahn-area indie club (now at Nobistor 14).
note: Evening venue — check programme.

name: Gruenspan
desc: Historic live club on Große Freiheit.
note: Evening venue — check programme.

name: Elbphilharmonie (Plaza)
desc: Concert hall on the harbour; the public Plaza viewing deck gives a great view over the port.
note: Plaza access normally needs a (free) timed ticket — check the site.
